What is currently happening in the market seemed impossible prior to today.

On a day where Nvidia, $NVDA, is down -6.5%, erasing -$300 billion in market cap, the Nasdaq 100 is now up +3.2%.

Even as the leader of not only the AI trade, but the broader market, accounting for nearly 8% of the S&P 500, falls sharply, investors are aggressively buying the dip.

Price action over the last 5 days has been a testament to just how powerful the AI Revolution truly is.

Investors are incredibly eager to buy the dip in US technology stocks, even if it means leaving the biggest leader of the AI Revolution behind.

In fact, the AI trade, and the market's rally as a whole, appears to be broadening.

Innovation is at an all-time high and markets know it.

This is the most resilient market in history.

We've heard for a couple years now that AI would take all the jobs. Here's are four things to consider: 

•Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, taking the three-month average to 137,000. Monthly job growth has averaged 86,000 this year, a significant recovery from the average loss of 7,000 jobs per month between May and December 2025.

•The unemployment rate is at a historically low 4.1%, and it's been below 4.5% for a record five straight years.

•The prime-age employment-population ratio is at 80.7%, higher than anything we saw in the 2000s or 2010s economic expansions. More people in their prime working-age years are working now than at any point during the last two expansions.

•The layoff rate (layoffs as a percent of the workforce) is just 1%, even lower than the 1.2-1.3% we saw in 2018-2019, when the labor market was exceptionally strong.

AI has unquestionably been inflationary this year.

So if all the building slows down, could that be a potential positive to the inflation backdrop? We've been on record the Fed would be significantly more dovish than what the Fed Funds Futures were pricing in and could this now say no more hikes?

BREAKING: 221 US trucking companies have filed for bankruptcy so far in 2026, on track for the highest annual total in 23 years.

This marks the 3rd consecutive year with at least 220 bankruptcies.

By comparison, annual bankruptcies were below 100 in both 2021 and 2022.

Furthermore, ~66% of small US trucking firms, typically operating 20 or fewer trucks, reported flat or declining revenue YoY, according to a Truckstop and Bloomberg survey of hundreds of carriers.

At the same time, ~40% expect to leave the industry or are unsure of their future over the next 6 months.

This comes as surging diesel prices, rising insurance premiums, and higher interest rates are increasingly squeezing smaller trucking companies.

The US trucking industry needs help.

BREAKING: US data center construction spending jumped +90% YoY in September, to a record annualized rate of $96.5 billion.

This also marks the largest YoY increase in 10 years.

This figure is now risen more than +60% YoY for 4 consecutive months.

Since the start of 2024, data center construction spending has nearly quadrupled.

Meanwhile, general office construction spending fell -8% YoY in September, to $46.0 billion, near its lowest level since January 2016.

This brought the gap between data center and general office construction spending to a record $50.5 billion.

Overall, US construction spending fell -1.9% MoM in September, its biggest monthly decline since April 2020.

The AI infrastructure buildout is transforming the US economy.

BREAKING: The US manufacturing sector added +19,000 jobs in October, its 3rd-largest monthly increase since November 2023.

This also marks the 5th consecutive monthly gain, the longest streak since 2022.

Over this period, the manufacturing sector has added +86,000 jobs, bringing total employment to 12.68 million, its highest since December 2024.

This follows a decline of -323,000 jobs between January 2023 and December 2025.

Despite the recent recovery, US manufacturing employment remains 222,000 jobs below its January 2023 level.

US manufacturing employment is seeing some much needed relief.
